name: Connecticut
summary: Connecticut allows one portable solar device of up to 1,200 watts behind your meter. Your electric company cannot require approval, charge a fee, or demand extra equipment.
watt_cap_note: Maximum output; one device per electric meter; plugs into a standard 120-volt outlet.
certification: Not confirmed. State building and fire codes are to add safe-installation provisions.

utility.fees: No approval, fees, or additional controls beyond what is built into the device.

renters: No landlord provision found. Ask your landlord in writing.
hoa: Not addressed in the sources we found.
open_questions: Signing date is reported as June 4 or July 15, 2026; the bill history shows the Public Act number assigned May 20, 2026.
